summary:
Astro-Lab — Landing on Mars is an interactive educational game developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, responding to the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer".

Designed for young learners, the project introduces players to Mars exploration through three playable missions: repairing a rover, analyzing Martian rock samples and navigating a meteor storm.

Each mission combines interactive gameplay with scientific learning activities. Players investigate the Martian environment, interact with mission equipment and complete a six-question science quiz to test their knowledge.

The experience includes keyboard and touchscreen controls, progress tracking, immediate quiz feedback and a final mission certificate summarizing the player's performance.

By combining exploration, gamification and space science, Astro-Lab aims to make planetary exploration more accessible and engaging, inspiring younger generations to discover STEM subjects and the challenges of human exploration on Mars.
details:
Astro-Lab — Landing on Mars

Project Overview

Astro-Lab is an interactive educational Mars exploration simulator designed for young learners. Developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, it responds to the challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer".

The experience places players in the role of an astronaut completing a simulated expedition on Mars. Through three different missions, players explore the Martian environment, interact with equipment and investigate scientific phenomena.

Missions

1. Repair the Rover

Players recover missing modules scattered across the Martian terrain to restore the rover's mobile laboratory. They must navigate the environment and avoid Dust Devils, which reduce the remaining mission time.

2. Analyze the Rocks

Players investigate three Martian rock samples by observing their texture, chemistry and geological origin. NASA imagery is integrated into the experience, with interactive zoom functionality to support visual investigation and scientific learning.

3. Meteor Storm

Players face a simulated meteor storm and use their spacesuit's seismograph to observe and interpret recorded impacts.

Educational System

Each mission concludes with a six-question science quiz. Players receive immediate feedback and earn points for correct answers.

A passing threshold of 60% is used to evaluate quiz performance. At the end of the experience, a final certificate summarizes the player's results and training progress.

Gameplay Features

  • Three playable missions.
  • Interactive astronaut movement and environmental interactions.
  • Mission objectives and time-based challenges.
  • Scientific investigation of Martian rocks.
  • Interactive quizzes with immediate feedback.
  • Score and progress tracking.
  • Final performance certificate.
  • Pause, resume and restart functionality.
  • Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
  • Responsive interface and accessibility features.

Technical Implementation

Astro-Lab was developed using JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, CSS3 and Vite.

The architecture uses native JavaScript ES Modules and separates the core engine, game systems, scenes, missions and visual components.

The graphics are primarily rendered programmatically through Canvas. Browser storage is used to preserve progress:

  • localStorage stores best mission results and scores.
  • sessionStorage preserves the mission currently in progress.

The interface supports desktop and mobile devices, keyboard and touch interactions, ARIA attributes and reduced-motion preferences.

Target Audience and Impact

The project is designed primarily for children and young learners interested in astronomy, space exploration and science.

Its educational approach combines interactive challenges with scientific information, helping players discover aspects of planetary exploration while developing curiosity and interest in STEM subjects.

Team

Astro-Lab was developed collaboratively by:

  • Federico Bosio — @bosioF
  • Lorenzo Borgogno — @L0ry-BR
  • Edoardo Crestani — @crestaniedoardo-jpg
  • Lorenzo Perassi — @perassilorenzo

The public repository contains the final project release, while collaborative development took place in a separate private repository.
